title: Phased control-plane rollout automation with traffic-shift gating
creator: Amaya Patel
description:
Goal: implement an automated, phased upgrade flow for Private (VPC) control-planes that lets operators roll forward a control-plane version across tenant clusters with minimal manual coordination and deterministic rollback triggers. Scope: Terraform/IaC modules for versioned control-plane resources, a lightweight orchestration shim to perform staged traffic-shifts, health gating based on kube-level and application-level SLOs, KV-cache warmup and compatibility checks, audit logging for upgrade events, and a runbook for operator failures.

Design highlights: use a versioned terraform module (controlplane_v2) that exposes: desired_version, staging_pool_tag, traffic_shift_percentage, preflight_checks (bool), and post_upgrade_hooks. The orchestration shim (stateless service) will read desired_version and pool tags, create new control-plane instances in the target VPC, run a health probe battery (kube-apiserver metrics, control-plane P99 latency, operator heartbeats, authn/authz smoke tests), and perform incremental traffic-shifts (5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%) with configurable wait windows and automatic rollback on threshold breaches.

Health gating: gating rules are driven by SLO thresholds stored in the Console; primary signals: control-plane api_5xx_rate, api_p99_latency, token_validation_errors, and kv-cache-hit-rate. We will instrument a composite upgrade_health signal and require a stable window (configurable, default 3m) before advancing.

Rollback/Failover: rollback is automated via Terraform rollback plan plus orchestration shim issuing immediate traffic-shift back to previous pool and invoking post_rollback_hooks. All state changes must be recorded in audit logs tied to customer tenancy and mirrored into the Console timeline for transparency.

Testing & rollout plan: end-to-end test harness in CI (staging) will simulate a multi-tenant VPC with traffic generator workload. We will run blue/green verification, then a phased rollout across internal customers, then invited beta customers before general availability.

Trade-offs and decisions: we avoided a full orchestration service that stores persistent state to reduce operational burden — instead the shim is stateless and uses Terraform state + tags as source-of-truth. This simplifies drift handling but requires strict locking on Terraform runs. We chose staged traffic-shift over simple single-canary because it offers finer control for high-risk customers and smoother capacity transitions.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Phased+Control+Plane+Rollout ; terraform module tree: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/infra/terraform-modules/-/tree/controlplane_v2 ; orchestration POC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/412 ; runbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xYf-runbook-draft
